The iron arches of the old suspension bridge groaned under the weight of the relentless downpour, a symphony of rust and tension that had played for over a century. Rain did not merely fall here; it descended in heavy, silver curtains, blurring the boundary between the churning river below and the mist-shrouded peaks above. Each drop struck the wet pavement with a rhythmic persistence, creating a mosaic of fleeting ripples that danced across the surface before vanishing into the dark abyss of the water. The bridge itself was a skeleton of riveted steel, painted in a shade of green that had long since surrendered to the elements, revealing patches of oxidized brown that looked like scars from a forgotten war.

Along the length of the span, lanterns hung from curved iron arms, their glass panes fogged by the humidity and the chill of the evening air. They flickered with a warm, amber glow, a stark contrast to the cold, blue-grey twilight that enveloped the valley. These lights were not merely functional; they were sentinels, guiding travelers through the gloom with a gentle, unwavering presence. As the wind picked up, swirling the rain into horizontal sheets, the flames within the lanterns danced wildly, casting long, distorted shadows that stretched and contracted across the wet asphalt. The light reflected off the puddles, creating a second, inverted world beneath the feet of those who dared to cross.

There was a profound solitude in this scene, a sense that the bridge existed outside of time, suspended in a perpetual moment of twilight and storm. The sound of the rain was deafening in its consistency, a white noise that drowned out the distant hum of the city and the whisper of the wind through the bare branches of the trees lining the riverbank
